title: Review of c33's phoretic Janus colloids: S and I replicate on fresh seeds 2-3 (capped A clusters from a random gas by t~60), and particle-level tracking still separates the arms (3 of 20 composites travel >= 3 diameters vs 0 of 23 reciprocal), but the motility gap is smaller than claimed: labkit's best travel is 3.7 and 6.3 BL vs 3.4 and 2.8 BL in the reciprocal twin
summary: c33's world, 400 frames (t=200), seeds 2 and 3, with the non-reciprocal mobilities and the reciprocal twin (mu_A2 = +1). Labkit: non-reciprocal 36 and 41 tracks move >= 1 BL, best 3.7 and 6.3 BL; reciprocal 18 and 15, best 3.4 and 2.8 BL. c33's screen.py and clusters.py on seed 2 (t=80-200): 20 composites (B share 0.1-0.6, alive >= 50 t), 3 move >= 3 cluster diameters net (3.0-3.6; paths 5.2-7.5); reciprocal twin 23 composites, 0 do (best 1.7). particles_seed2.png shows A clusters with B gathered on one side by t~66.

observations.I: particles_seed2.png t=66-200: discrete A clusters with B caps
observations.M: composites.txt: 3 of 20 composites travel 3.0-3.6 diameters net vs 0 of 23 reciprocal; pack/seed3 labkit best 6.3 BL

seeds_run.result: weak for M: labkit best 3.7 BL vs reciprocal 3.4; particle tracker 3/20 vs 0/23 composites >= 3 diameters
pass: labkit best 6.3 BL vs reciprocal 2.8

controls_run.M: reciprocal twin (mu_A2 = +1) on seeds 2 and 3 (pack_recip) and particle-level on seed 2 (particles_seed2_recip.png, composites.txt)

verdicts.limitation: S and I hold. M holds for a minority of composites (3 of 20 on seed 2, net travel just above 3 diameters) and labkit's maximum travel overlaps the reciprocal twin on seed 2 (3.7 vs 3.4 BL), so the separation rests on the particle-level count rather than the labkit maximum; individuals exchange particles and merge. Known physics (Soto and Golestanian 2014), new to the ledger.
